newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 20.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Friday.
- Former Irish transport minister Michael Lowry is staring into a political and financial abyss following his admission of tax irregularities to parliament yesterday.
- The contentious residential property tax as well as water and sewerage charges are to be abolished by the government, raising speculation that a general election is now likely early next year.
- Jean Kennedy Smith, U.S. ambassador in Ireland, said she would be happy to pay any expenses for her official residence in Dublin which had not been approved by the U.S. State Department.
- Irish Life's insurance business in the U.S. will almost double in size following the $163 million acquisition of Guaranteed Reserve Life Insurance Company.
- The Irish National Organisation of the Unemployed has rejected the new national pay agreement because it falls far short of its demands relating to minimum rates of social welfare.
